whole_original_native_metadata.title: A credited finiteness deduction for restricted boundary-twist factorizations
whole_original_native_metadata.description: For each fixed genus g ≥ 1, let S(g,1) be an oriented compact surface with one boundary component, and let maps and isotopies fix that boundary pointwise. We prove that ordered positive factorizations of one positive boundary Dehn twist, along non-null-homotopic simple closed curves with repetitions permitted and pairwise geometric intersection at most one, have finitely many simultaneous-conjugacy classes. Their maximal length M(g) is finite and attained, with M(g) ≥ 4g(2g+1). Peripheral factors occur only in the singleton factorization; otherwise all factors are nonseparating. The values M(1) = 12 and M(2) = 40 are credited deductions from prior work with the convention bridge stated. This gives a complete negative answer, under the stated conventions, to the separately printed restricted arbitrary-length clause in the Wajnryb/Farb problem collection. The full original maximum and classification bundle remains partial: exact M(g) for g ≥ 3, explicit upper formulas, an effective exhaustive-enumeration stopping criterion, extremizers, and Hurwitz, positive Artin, T-move and A5/D6 classifications remain unresolved in this work. The note is a credited deduction and exposition. Cossu and Tringali's arXiv:2208.05869v3, Corollary 4.13, supplies the generic finite-alphabet finiteness corollary through a normal reduced cone and nonerasing atomic expansions. The support and ribbon arguments explicitly build on Juvan–Malnič–Mohar, Malestein–Rivin–Theran, and Cahn–Fanoni–Petri. Honda–Kazez–Matić, Smith, the chain relation, and Baykur–Monden–Van Horn-Morris provide credited premises. Exact historical priority of the resulting surface application, novelty, and worldwide current-open status remain UNKNOWN; a bounded literature audit is not an absence proof. Extensive AI tools were used in mathematical and source checking, writing, code, and package preparation. This preprint is unrefereed, has no external human peer review, and is not formally certified. The accompanying verification kit provides written proof and source/custody records plus reproducible finite fault controls; those controls do not replace the universal proof or replay omitted historical inputs.

printed_title: A credited finiteness deduction for restricted boundary-twist factorizations
printed_original_abstract_whole_TeX: Fix an oriented compact surface of genus $g\geq1$ with one boundary circle, and fix that boundary pointwise in both maps and isotopies. Ordered positive factorizations of its single boundary twist, along non-null-homotopic simple closed curves with pairwise geometric intersection at most one, have finitely many simultaneous-conjugacy classes. Repetitions are permitted. Their lengths therefore have a finite attained maximum $M(g)$, with $4g(2g+1)\leq M(g)$; credited low-genus deductions give $M(1)=12$ and $M(2)=40$. This is a credited finiteness deduction and exposition: the finite-alphabet group lemma is a verified corollary of Cossu--Tringali's factorization theory, and the support and embedding mechanisms are prior curve-system and ribbon-surface methods, with the marked bordered adaptation supplied here. It answers negatively the separately stated restricted arbitrary-length clause attributed to Smith in Wajnryb's chapter. Exact $M(g)$ for $g\geq3$, explicit upper formulas, a stopping criterion, extremizers and finer classifications remain unresolved in this work. Historical novelty and exact priority are not certified.
